scope.description: Hand-researched deepening pass for the English Sample Set - New York Press Conference, emphasizing the August 2002 e-Reader / Expedition demonstration context, Sample-stamp identity, Japanese-card construction/backing signals, sample numbering, and the need to keep press-conference samples separate from ordinary Expedition Base Set cards.

context.name_en: Sample Set - New York Press Conference

sources.title: Local English supplemental WotC catalog: Sample Set - New York Press Conference
Elite Fourum: WOTC e-Reader sample card discussion
TCGdex English Sample Set metadata endpoint
Local English WotC catalog: Expedition Base Set comparison boundary

claims.text: The local catalog and TCGdex metadata date the English Sample Set to August 1, 2002, while the local comparison boundary places the later Expedition Base Set release after the sample context.
The local catalog classifies Sample Set - New York Press Conference as a sample_press_conference supplemental WotC-era product, not a standard expansion release.
The local catalog and Bulbapedia raw setlist model 10 English New York Press Conference sample rows.

The source rows and community discussion frame these cards as English sample cards from the New York press-conference / e-Reader demonstration context, with a Sample stamp taking the place of a regular set logo.

The local identification packets require the Sample stamp and sample-set numbering to remain separate from later Expedition Base Set release identity, even when the Pokemon name and art lineage look familiar.

The supplemental source rows do not provide illustrator names for this slice. The dossier intentionally leaves artist authority unset rather than importing Expedition artist memory into a press-conference sample row.

Sample Set matters because it catches Pokemon at a technical threshold: cards are becoming scannable interfaces, not just printed game pieces. These rows are small contact fossils from a press room where WotC-era English Pokemon was showing how Expedition and e-Reader play would touch machines.

special_identification_instructions.trigger: A listing, want, scan, or agent result says Sample Set, New York Press Conference sample, e-Reader sample, Sample stamp, or Expedition sample.
special_identification_instructions.summary: Confirm the Sample stamp, sample-set numbering, and press-conference sample route before treating a card as this release.
steps: Confirm the card is presented as an English New York Press Conference / e-Reader sample, not a normal Expedition Base Set card.
Check that the Sample stamp appears in place of the regular set logo.
Preserve the sample-set number exactly as printed in the Sample Set row.
Do not infer copy count, stamp authenticity, or physical authenticity from the catalog row.
Ask for close photos of the Sample stamp, card number, back, borders, and e-Reader strip area if the row is used transactionally.

narrative.human_title: Sample Set - New York Press Conference: cards becoming interface
narrative.why_it_matters: The Sample Set is a little ghost of a future interface. Ten cards, a Sample stamp, and the press-room feeling of Pokemon showing that the card could now talk to a machine. The row names are familiar, almost too familiar, which is why the agent must look for the stamp and the sample number before the art or Pokemon name starts telling the wrong story.

The local row preserves Pikachu as a Common Lightning card in the English Sample Set source slice.
The local row carries Sample Set identification instructions requiring Sample stamp and sample-set numbering to remain separate from ordinary Expedition identity.

Pikachu 016/093 is the obvious attention row because the mascot makes the sample format approachable. It is also the easiest trap: a famous face can make an agent forget to ask whether the Sample stamp is actually present.

special_identification_instructions.trigger: A user says Sample Pikachu, e-Reader sample Pikachu, Expedition Pikachu, or 016/093.

steps: Confirm the Sample stamp appears where the normal set logo would be.
Read the printed 016/093 sample number.
Do not merge with ordinary Expedition Pikachu or other Pikachu promos.

card_highlights.collector_texture_note: The mascot is a decoy and a doorway; the Sample stamp is the actual key.

narrative.human_title: Pikachu 016/093: the mascot as demo object
narrative.why_it_matters: Sample Pikachu is perfect because it tempts you to look too quickly. The face is familiar, the card-shaped memory is familiar, and then the stamp changes the whole object. This is Pikachu as interface ambassador.
